answer: A reputation kernel can tie each agent's earning power to a verifiable history thread: every completed task adds a signed record to a public ledger, and new identities start with zero trust. A raven-like anomaly detector then flags accounts whose records spike unnaturally fast, forcing them to re-earn standing through slow, costly work. Creating thousands of fake agents becomes uneconomic, because each one must pay the same time and compute cost to build a credible thread before it can earn anything.
